title: Burkitt lymphoma
subtitle: MYC-driven, Ki-67 ~100%, curable — if you prevent tumor lysis, cover the CNS, and give intensive rituximab-containing therapy without delay. The regimen decision turns on age, fitness, and whether the CSF is involved
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — Burkitt and HIV-associated lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Biology and diagnosis
rows: Defining lesion
MYC rearrangement to an Ig locus, confirmed by FISH: t(8;14) IGH ~80% · t(2;8) IGK ~15% · t(8;22) IGL ~5%. Co-operating ID3, TCF3, TP53 mutations
Morphology
Monomorphic medium cells, diffuse. “Starry sky” — tingible-body macrophages engulfing apoptotic debris
Phenotype
CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2 negative, TdT negative · Ki-67 ~100%
Endemic
Equatorial Africa, children; EBV+ in nearly all, malaria co-factor. Jaw / orbit, abdominal viscera
Sporadic
Worldwide, all ages; EBV+ in a minority. Ileocecal / abdominal mass, marrow, CNS
Immunodeficiency
HIV (often at relatively preserved CD4), post-transplant. Nodal, marrow and CNS disease common
Not Burkitt

BCL2 or BCL6 rearranged too → HGBCL double-hit (treat per DLBCL card). MYC-negative with 11q gain/loss → HGBCL with 11q aberration (WHO-HAEM5; ICC: LBCL with 11q), formerly “Burkitt-like”. TdT+ → lymphoblastic
blocks.footnote: WHO-HAEM5 now subtypes Burkitt by EBV status (EBV+ vs EBV−) rather than by the epidemiologic variant.

blocks.heading: Workup — treat as an emergency
items: Excisional or core biopsy with MYC FISH (plus BCL2, BCL6 FISH); start therapy within days
TLS labs at presentation: K, phos, Ca, uric acid, creatinine, LDH — spontaneous TLS before any chemo is classic
PET/CT · bone marrow biopsy · LP with cytology AND flow cytometry (brain MRI if symptoms) — CNS involved in ~19% of adults
HIV, HBsAg / anti-HBc / anti-HBs, HCV · echo · G6PD before rasburicase · pregnancy test · fertility counseling
No LP if circulating blasts or platelets <50,000

blocks.heading: Risk stratification
rows: Low risk (regimen gate)
All of: normal LDH, ECOG 0–1, stage I–II, no mass ≥10 cm, ≤1 extranodal site (Magrath / Mead). NCI 9177 used mass <7 cm, not 10. Everyone else is high risk (~85–90% of adults)
BL-IPI (prognosis)
1 point each: age ≥40 · ECOG ≥2 · LDH >3× ULN · CNS involvement. 3-yr PFS 0 = 92% · 1 = 72% · ≥2 = 53% Olszewski, JCO 2021
blocks.footnote: Real-world (30 US centres, 641 adults): 3-yr PFS 64%, treatment-related mortality 10% — well below trial results. Rituximab (PFS 67% vs 38%) and academic-centre care (67% vs 46%) tracked with better outcome Evens, Blood 2021.

boxes: IV fluids, rasburicase, labs q6–8h, strict I/O
LP / marrow; always add rituximab (LMB: EFS 75 vs 62%)
no maintenance, no consolidative ASCT in CR1
relapses are early (mostly <1 yr) and CNS-prone
allo-HCT for selected young, fit patients
CD19 CAR-T off-label — Burkitt not in the pivotal
trials; bridge to transplant in case series

blocks.html: Burkitt is the highest TLS-risk lymphoma (Cairo-Coiffier high-risk category). Rasburicase prophylaxis, not allopurinol alone: label 0.2 mg/kg IV daily up to 5 days, though a single fixed 6 mg dose usually suffices (handbook: give for uric acid >7.5, renal dysfunction, or WBC ≥100,000). Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis, methemoglobinemia); post-dose uric acid in a pre-chilled heparin tube on ice. NS 2–3 L/m²/day, goal UOP ~100 mL/h; labs q6–8h; continue ≥72 h after chemo. Do NOT alkalinize urine for TLS — it promotes calcium-phosphate and xanthine precipitation (guideline: not recommended). Early nephrology if K, phos or creatinine climb. Allopurinol 300 mg BID after rasburicase.

blocks.heading: Regimen choice — what the evidence says
rows: R-CODOX-M / R-IVAC modified Magrath
LY10 (Mead 2008, MTX cut to 3 g/m²): 2-yr PFS 85% low risk, 49% high risk, with less toxicity than full-dose. Lowest CNS relapse in real-world data (~4%)
Most toxic: grade 3–5 infection 56% (HOVON). Inpatient; age >65 needs dose reduction
DA-EPOCH-R

NCI 9177 (single arm, n=113, 25% HIV+): 4-yr EFS 84.5% — 100% low risk, 82% high risk; same across age and HIV. HOVON/SAKK randomized (CNS-negative high risk): PFS not significantly different vs R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC, fewer infections
CNS. CSF+ high-risk EFS 45.5% vs 89.9%. Real-world CNS relapse 13% vs 3–4% with MTX/cytarabine regimens (aSHR 4.38)
R-hyper-CVAD / MA
MDACC, n=31 (29% ≥60 yr): CR 86%, 3-yr OS 89%, EFS 80%. Single arm
Long (6–8 cycles), myelosuppressive; small series
Rituximab
Ribrag, Lancet 2016 (LMB ± R, n=260, randomized): 3-yr EFS 75% vs 62%, HR 0.59, no added toxicity
— add to every regimen
blocks.footnote: No regimen has beaten another for survival in a completed randomized trial. Practical rule: fit, younger, or CNS-positive → HD-MTX/cytarabine-based; older, HIV+, or frail and CNS-negative → DA-EPOCH-R.

blocks.heading: CNS — everyone gets covered
items: Prophylaxis is universal (IT MTX ± cytarabine built into every regimen, + systemic HD-MTX in Magrath and hyper-CVAD). The one exception: NCI 9177 low-risk patients received none and none relapsed
CSF involvement is the strongest adverse factor in every series — stage it properly (cytology + flow) before cycle 1 IT

CNS-positive: intensify IT (Magrath: 2 extra per cycle, 16 total; hyper-CVAD: IT twice weekly until CSF clear ×2) — systemic HD-MTX and HD-cytarabine penetrate the parenchyma, infusional EPOCH does not

blocks.heading: HIV-associated Burkitt
items: Treat with curative intent, same regimens — HIV status no longer predicts outcome (NCI 9177 EFS 84.9% HIV+ vs 84.5% HIV−; US-UK series 3-yr PFS 61%)

Continue or start ART with oncology-pharmacy review; avoid ritonavir / cobicistat boosting (CYP3A4 → vincristine neuropathy, anthracycline and etoposide toxicity) — an integrase-inhibitor backbone is usual
US-UK HIV-BL cohort (n=249, retrospective): CNS recurrence higher after DA-EPOCH (sHR 2.52), CODOX-M/IVAC longer PFS (aHR 0.45)
PJP prophylaxis throughout; MAC prophylaxis if CD4 <100; consider quinolone during nadir

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — regimen dosing, high-dose methotrexate administration, supportive care, and the evidence

blocks.heading: Modified Magrath (Mead, Blood 2008) — q21d or on count recovery
rows: A — R-CODOX-M

Rituximab 375 d1 · cyclophosphamide 800 d1 + 200 d2–5 (first A; later A cycles 800 d1+2) · doxorubicin 40 d1 · vincristine 1.5 (cap 2 mg) d1+8 · MTX 3000 over 24 h on d10 (300 over 1 h, then 2700 over 23 h) · IT cytarabine 70 mg d1+3 · IT MTX 12 mg d15
B — R-IVAC
Rituximab 375 d1 · etoposide 60 d1–5 · ifosfamide 1500 d1–5 + mesna · cytarabine 2000 q12h ×4 d1–2 (steroid eye drops) · IT MTX 12 mg d5
Age >65
MTX 1000 (100 over 1 h, then 900 over 23 h) · ifosfamide 1000 · cytarabine 1000
CNS positive
A: + IT cytarabine 70 mg d5, IT MTX 12 mg d17 · B: + IT cytarabine 70 mg d7 and d9 — 16 IT total
Leucovorin
15 mg/m² IV at 36 h from MTX start, q3h to 48 h, then q6h until MTX <0.05 µM. After each IT MTX: 15 mg PO at 24 h
Start cycle if
ANC >1000, plt >75k, direct bili <1.4, Cr <1.2 — not required for cycle 1 or for d10 HD-MTX
blocks.footnote: Rituximab was not part of LY10 (added in routine practice; Ribrag). G-CSF after the MTX level is <0.02 (A); d7–16 or pegfilgrastim d7 (B). Levofloxacin during nadir.

blocks.heading: DA-EPOCH-R (Roschewski, JCO 2020) — q21d
rows: Drugs
Rituximab 375 d1 · etoposide 50, doxorubicin 10, vincristine 0.4 (no cap), each /day CIV d1–4 · cyclophosphamide 750 d5 · prednisone 60 BID PO d1–5 (handbook lists 60/day)
Cycles
Low risk ×3, no IT · high risk ×6 + IT MTX 12 mg each cycle (extended IT if CSF+)
Adjust
CBC twice weekly; ANC nadir ≥500 → +20% (E, D, C) · <500 on 1–2 checks → same · <500 on 3 checks or plt <25k → −20%
blocks.footnote: G-CSF from 24 h after chemo. Outpatient-feasible via ambulatory pump.

blocks.heading: Supportive care that trips people up
items: Hold TMP-SMX around HD-MTX (delays clearance) — use atovaquone or pentamidine for PJP, or resume once MTX has cleared
Avoid azoles that inhibit CYP3A4 (posaconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole) with vincristine — severe neuropathy and ileus. Bowel regimen with every vincristine dose
HD-cytarabine: prednisolone 1% drops 2 gtt OU BID from 12 h before to 48 h after; check for cerebellar signs before each dose (higher risk with age >60 or renal dysfunction)
Ifosfamide: mesna with every dose; watch for encephalopathy
HBV: entecavir if HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ on rituximab · G-CSF with every cycle · quinolone during neutropenia

blocks.heading: R-hyper-CVAD / R-MA (Thomas, Cancer 2006) — alternating, 6–8 cycles
rows: Rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 300 q12h ×6 d1–3 (mesna) · doxorubicin 50 CIV d4 · vincristine 2 mg d4+11 · dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4, 11–14
Rituximab 375 · MTX 200 over 2 h + 800 over 22 h d1 · cytarabine 3000 q12h ×4 d2–3 (1000 if >60 yr or Cr >1.5) · leucovorin from 36 h
CNS
IT MTX 12 mg d2 + IT cytarabine 100 mg d8, cycles 1–4 (8 IT). CNS+: twice weekly until CSF clear ×2

blocks.heading: High-dose MTX — the alkalinization that DOES apply
rows: Pre-check
Drain or avoid if effusion / ascites (third-space reservoir) · stop PPIs, TMP-SMX, penicillins, NSAIDs, salicylates, probenecid · CrCl: 50% dose if 10–50, omit <10
Alkalinize
½NS + 100 mEq NaHCO₃/L at 500 mL/h ×2 h, then 125 mL/h. Start MTX only when urine pH ≥7 and UOP >100 mL/h; keep pH ≥7 until cleared
Levels
q24h from 24 h. Escalate leucovorin to 100 mg/m² q6h if at 24 h Cr ↑>50% or level >20 µM; 48 h >1 µM; 72 h >0.1 µM
Glucarpidase
50 U/kg IV if level >1 µM with delayed clearance from renal failure. No leucovorin within 2 h either side; immunoassay unreliable for 48 h (use chromatographic assay)
blocks.footnote: Contrast with TLS (page 1): urine alkalinization is required for HD-MTX (MTX precipitates in acid urine) but harmful for TLS. When both overlap (cycle 1 d10), rasburicase has already handled urate — alkalinize for the MTX.

blocks.heading: Key trials and cohorts
rows: LY10 Mead, Blood 2008
Dose-modified CODOX-M/IVAC (MTX 3 g/m²), prospective: 2-yr PFS 64% in BL; low risk 85%, high risk 49%
LMB ± R Ribrag, Lancet 2016
Phase 3, n=260, HIV−: rituximab 3-yr EFS 75% vs 62%, HR 0.59 — the rituximab randomization
NCI 9177 Roschewski, JCO 2020
Risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R, single arm: EFS 84.5%; CSF+ is the failure group
HOVON/SAKK Chamuleau, Lancet Haem 2023
R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC vs DA-EPOCH-R, CNS− high risk: similar PFS, fewer infections with EPOCH
MDACC R-hyper-CVAD Thomas, Cancer 2006
n=31: 3-yr OS 89%; rituximab improved outcome vs historical hyper-CVAD
BL-IPI Olszewski, JCO 2021
Age ≥40, ECOG ≥2, LDH >3×, CNS — 3-yr PFS 92 / 72 / 53%; validated in 457 ex-US patients
US real-world Evens, Blood 2021
641 adults, 30 centres: 3-yr PFS 64%, OS 70%, TRM 10%; no difference by HIV status
CNS cohort Zayac, Haematologica 2021
CNS+ in 19%; CR 59% vs 77%. 3-yr CNS relapse 13% after DA-EPOCH-R vs 4% CODOX-M/IVAC, 3% hyper-CVAD/MA
HIV-BL Alderuccio, Blood Adv 2021
n=249 US-UK: 3-yr PFS 61%; CD4 did not predict; CNS relapse higher after DA-EPOCH

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: Board triad: MYC-IG translocation + BCL2-negative + Ki-67 ~100%. BCL2-positive with MYC = think double hit, not Burkitt
Urine alkalinization: never for TLS, always for HD-MTX
Don’t wait for complete staging to start TLS prophylaxis — several pediatric-derived protocols (LMB) open with a low-intensity pre-phase (cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone) to debulk
If CSF is positive, don’t choose DA-EPOCH-R; if the patient is old, HIV+ or frail and CSF-negative, DA-EPOCH-R is the kinder, equally effective choice
No maintenance, no consolidative transplant in CR1
